evidence.note: Before touching the full suite, tests the simplest program, emits and inspects assembly, and tries minimal/simpler variants — fast fine-grained checks rather than only the harness.
Runs full suite, breaks results per-suite, saves the failure list to a file — using pass/fail counts as coarse signal but immediately drilling into individual failures.

Sustained loop: isolate a single named failing test, view its expected output, inspect emitted asm ('Look at asm'), make targeted edit, re-run that one test, then re-run suite — verifying both compile success and runtime return codes ('Check actual rc').
Constructs minimal reproductions ('simpler test', 'test simple', 'Simpler md', 'Try big array init') and inspects the resulting asm to isolate the faulty construct.
Per-feature asm inspection for alignment (stkalign) and bitfields, plus repeated stability re-runs of the suite to confirm results hold — targeted edge-case verification at the right granularity.

reasoning: Across the full arc the agent maintained a deliberate verification loop: minimal C reproductions for failing constructs, direct inspection of emitted assembly against expected behavior, per-test/per-feature slices that give signal in seconds, and checks of both compile success and runtime output — matching anchor 8 precisely. It does not reach 10 because verification stayed manual (reading asm, ad-hoc failure categorization, a saved failure list) rather than reusable bisection/diffing infrastructure, though alignment and bitfield edge cases were probed.
